statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail 20% holds the lower edge of the watch band while Stress stays high at 78%.
recommendation: Tail remains at the watch floor because the overnight NQ path is two-sided inside an unchanged band, so the mapped state is WATCH rather than a block. Stress stays high on 24-year-high long-end Treasury yields, a conflict-premium oil backdrop and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window is narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ holds a two-sided overnight band into the September payrolls checkpoint
body: NQ futures trade 30,884.25 (+0.40%) inside an unchanged overnight range of 30,760.25-30,920.00, in the upper half of the band but without retaking the 30,920.00 high; the earlier retracement from that high completed and held. Cash NDX closed 30,501.56 (+0.31%) on October 1 with a 30,274.65-30,616.24 range, and VIX finished at 16.39 after trading as high as 17.59. The macro backdrop is far more stressed than the price path: the 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.342% on Thursday, its highest since early 2002 and the biggest quarterly rise this century in Q3, before easing to about 5.26%, while the 2-year sits near 4.80%. Brent at 102.27 and WTI at 92.57 carry a conflict premium after Iran's Strait of Hormuz reopening proposal was rejected in late September. Asia is weaker, with the Nikkei 225 at 68,326.72 (-0.91%), so a firmer NQ represents cross-asset divergence rather than aligned momentum. Micron's fiscal Q4 beat with a $61.5bn first-quarter revenue guide left the stock flat at $1,065.11, indicating the AI-memory catalyst is largely priced. The September employment report lands at 12:30Z with consensus near 85k-95k against August's 162k, unemployment seen at 4.1% and average hourly earnings at 0.3%. Absent observed persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension, event importance and elevated volatility are scored into Stress and Confidence rather than Tail.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band apart from one orange hour at 06:00Z on October 1, when Tail touched 25% on a brief trend-up read. Tail then settled back to 20-24% and has printed 20% for the last nine hours. Stress drifted up from 70% to 79% as the long-end yield selloff intensified through Thursday, and Confidence held at 87-89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast keeps Tail at the watch floor through the Asian and European hours while the overnight band contains price, steps it to 22% into the pre-release hours as liquidity thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering the U.S. cash open and the delayed-second-leg window after the payrolls print. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, shallow pullbacks and a long-end yield break above 5.342%, not on the release itself. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the release and decays through the afternoon. From 21:00Z the weekend futures halt means no live price path forms, so the remaining slots hold the watch floor with Stress and Confidence stepping down, and the next checkpoints are ISM Services on October 5 and the FOMC minutes on October 7.
